response.rationale: R5 is the champion because it has the most direct support from the histopathological findings, including necrosis of vessel walls and focal fibrinoid necrosis, which are characteristic of Cutaneous Vasculitis. R4 is the runner-up because it also has support from the same histopathological findings, but the label Cutaneous Leukocytoclastic Vasculitis is less specific and does not fully capture the range of findings presented in the case.

rejected.why: Erythema Induratum is a type of lobular panniculitis, but the histopathological findings in this case do not support this diagnosis.
Wegener's Granulomatosis is a type of vasculitis that typically involves the upper and lower respiratory tracts and kidneys, but the findings in this case are limited to the skin.
Lupus Vasculitis is a possible diagnosis, but the findings in this case are not specific enough to support this diagnosis over other types of vasculitis.
Polyarteritis Nodosa is a type of vasculitis that typically involves medium-sized vessels, but the findings in this case are limited to the skin and do not support this diagnosis.
